traits: Every move uses one ease, steep at the start and level at the end, so entrances, exits and travels all feel cut from the same rule.
Nothing bounces: elements arrive on a mask and stop exactly on their mark.
Timings are multiples of one beat (125 ms), so arrivals line up with each other across the frame.
Scenes change by a wipe or a split along a straight edge, or by a hard cut.

notLike.line: proof also never bounces but its entrances are quick and varied and every cut is hard; grid keeps one ease throughout and lets a wipe or split edge cross the frame.
kinetic overshoots and slams; grid is rigid and stops on its mark with no overshoot at all.

nativeMoves.move: A mask reveal along a ruled edge: a headline or plate is uncovered by a straight line, as if drawn on a sheet.
nativeMoves.transfer: A site-survey film for a construction bid, each measured dimension uncovered along its own edge.

nativeMoves.move: A split cut at the climax: the frame divides along a line and the next scene is already behind it.
nativeMoves.transfer: A before-and-after film for a clinic, the cut line running down the middle as the second state slides in.

nativeMoves.move: Staggered arrivals on an even 62 ms step, so a row of items lands as a ruler of ticks.
nativeMoves.transfer: A timetable film where each departure appears in its column one tick after the last.

pitfalls.mistake: Adding a springy or overshooting entrance to a grid film.
pitfalls.mechanism: Everything else sits on a straight edge and stops dead; one element that wobbles past its mark breaks the alignment the viewer is reading.
pitfalls.fix: Keep overshoot at zero; use mask-reveal and rise, and move emphasis into the colour.

pitfalls.mistake: Holding scenes longer than about two seconds with no arrivals.
pitfalls.mechanism: The style gets its tension from steady ticks; a long still frame reads as stalled, not as calm.
pitfalls.fix: Add an arrival every second or so, or shorten the scene.

pitfalls.mistake: Mixing in curved eases for some elements.
pitfalls.mechanism: The single shared ease is what makes the film feel rule-bound; a softer curve on one item reads as a mistake.
pitfalls.fix: Use the style's enter, exit and move eases as given.

free: Which entrance (mask-reveal or rise) carries each text role.
Which scene gets the split and which the wipe, within the topic and climax roles.
The column and row structure of the layouts.
Scene length around the 1 second hold floor.
invariants: One ease for enter, exit and move.
Durations stay on the 125 ms step.
Cuts are wipes, splits or hard cuts, never a dissolve.
